The House met at eleven of the clock, 
MR. CHAIRMAN in the Chair. 
OBITUARY REFERENCE 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Hon. Members, I refer with profound sorrow 
to the passing away of Shri Devi Lal, a sitting Member of this House 
and former Deputy Prime Minister on 6 th April, 2001 at the age of 86 
following a cardiac arrest. 
Born in village Chautala, Haryana in September, 1914, Shri 
Devi Lal had his education at the Dev Samaj High School, Monga. 
An agriculturist by vocation, Shri Devi Lal actively took part in 
the freedom struggle of the country  and participated in the Civil 
Disobedience and Quit india Movements at the calf of Gandhiji in 
1929. He was at the forefront of several peasant movements during 
his political career spanning over five decades. 
Affectionately called 'Tau', Shri Devi Lal was a firm believer in 
the Gandhian philosophy of uplifting of rural masses. He devoted his 
life to the cause and the welfare of  farmers and villagers, He was a 
leader of the masses and the inte rest of the farmers was always 
uppermost in his mind. 
Shri Devi Lal had a long and distinguished political career 
starting with the membership of undivided Punjab Legislative 
Assembly, from 1952 to 1967. In 1963, he became the Leader of the 
Opposition in the Punjab Legislative Assembly. With the creation of 
the State of Haryana, he became  a Member of the Haryana 
Legislative Assembly in 1974, 1977,  1982, 1985 and again from 1987 
to 1989. During that period, he also served as the Chief Minister of 
Haryana from 1977 to 1980 and again from 1987 to 1989. 
Shri Devi Lal was a Member of the 7th and 9th Lok Sabhas and 
represented the State of Haryana in this House from 1998 till he 
breathed his last. He had the distinction of serving as the Deputy 
Prime Minister of India from 1989 to 1991. He was the President of the 
Janata Dal Parliamentary Board and the Samajwadi Party from 1980 
to 1984 and from 1991 to 1995 respectively.

RAJYA SABHA [16 April, 2001] 
In the passing away of Shri Devi Lal, the country has lost a 
veteran freedom fighter, an eminent parliamentarian, an able 
administrator and a crusader for the farmers' cause, 
We deeply mourn the passing away of Shri Devi Lal. I request 
the Members to rise in their places and observe silence as a mark of 
respect to the memory of the departed. 
(Hon. Members then stood in silence for one minute) 
MR. CHAIRMAN: The Secretary- General will convey to the 
members of the bereaved family our sense of profound sorrow and 
deep sympathy. 
As a mark of respect to the memory of Shri Devi Lal, a sitting 
Member and former Deputy Prime Minister, the House stands 
adjourned till 11 a.m. on Tuesday, the 17th April, 2001. 
The House then adjourned at three minutes past eleven of the 
clock, till eleven of the clock on Tuesday, the 17th April, 
2001.
